# omni_user_attribute_value (Resource)

One attribute value on one existing user, and nothing else about that user.

Use this for people Terraform does not own: users who sign in on their own, were invited from the UI, or are provisioned by something else. The user is looked up, not created, so destroying this resource clears the one key and leaves the person in place. Their other attributes, name and groups are never touched.

Written with a SCIM `PATCH` naming only this key, so it works on any user. It is also the way to set an attribute that takes multiple values, which `omni_user.attributes` cannot express.

Do not set the same key on the same user here and in `omni_user.attributes`. The two would overwrite each other, and `omni_user` replaces the whole user on every update.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A person Terraform does not own: they signed in on their own, so look them
# up instead of declaring an omni_user, which would deprovision them on destroy.
data "omni_user" "store_manager" {
  user_name = "store.manager@example.com"
}

# The definition can live in Terraform too.
resource "omni_user_attribute" "location_id" {
  name            = "location_id"
  label           = "Location"
  type            = "String"
  multiple_values = true
}

# The stores this person may see. Topic access filters key off location_id.
resource "omni_user_attribute_value" "store_manager_locations" {
  user_id = data.omni_user.store_manager.id
  name    = omni_user_attribute.location_id.name
  values  = ["123", "456"]
}

# A single-valued attribute takes value instead of values.
resource "omni_user_attribute_value" "store_manager_region" {
  user_id = data.omni_user.store_manager.id
  name    = "region"
  value   = "anz"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) The attribute's **Reference** value from **Settings > User attributes**, for example `location_id`. Use `omni_user_attribute.<name>.name` to make the attribute definition a dependency.
- `user_id` (String) The user's id, from `data.omni_user.<name>.id` for someone Terraform does not own or `omni_user.<name>.id` for someone it does.

### Optional

- `value` (String) The value, for an attribute that takes a single value. Exactly one of `value` or `values`. Numbers are given as strings.
- `values` (Set of String) The values, for an attribute created with `multiple_values = true`. Exactly one of `value` or `values`. Order does not matter. To clear every value, destroy the resource rather than setting an empty set.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) `<user_id>/<name>`.
